AFCS 1101.name: Introduction to African American and Africana Studies
AFCS 1101.rationale: The description introduces the interdisciplinary field of African American and Africana studies; this supports a broad cultural/social subject classification without assigning a narrower historical specialty.

AFCS 2600.guard: communities of color in the United States and internationally
AFCS 2600.name: Issues in Race, Science, and Technology
AFCS 2600.rationale: The description examines social and racial impacts of computing, biological and physical technologies on communities; it does not teach those technologies as a technical curriculum.

AFCS 3210.guard: from the 16th century to the present
AFCS 3210.name: Black Abolition Studies: Carcerality, Liberation, and Resistance
AFCS 3210.rationale: Historical and contemporary Black abolition, political organizing and resistance to carceral institutions are the substantive social/political subject.

BINF 6200.guard: Python and R as the main programming language
BINF 6200.name: Bioinformatics Programming
BINF 6200.rationale: The source explicitly teaches Python/R programming, data structures, object-oriented design, testing and implementation. Bioinformatics is the industry context, not a reason to suppress the foundational computing content.

BINF 6310.guard: exploratory data analysis of large-scale biological data
BINF 6310.name: Introduction to Bioinformatics
BINF 6310.rationale: The detailed source substantially combines biological sequence analysis and molecular/sequencing concepts with general command-line, Linux, DevOps/version-control and pipeline skills. No defensible single primary category is imposed; explicit mixed foundations and biological-domain content is preserved.

BIOC 1000.name: Biochemistry at Northeastern
BIOC 1000.rationale: First-year orientation to resources, academic skills, faculty and experiential options does not establish a substantive biochemistry subject inventory.

BIOL 1000.name: Biology at Northeastern
BIOL 1000.rationale: The description centers on student orientation, university resources and academic/professional skills; it does not specify a substantive biology methods curriculum.

BIOL 1107.guard: evolutionary principles, cellular structure and function
BIOL 1107.name: Foundations of Biology
BIOL 1107.rationale: Evolution, cell structure/function, genetics, energy pathways and physiology are biological-science domain content.

BIOL 1108.guard: genetic transmission, energy pathways, and physiology
BIOL 1108.name: Lab for BIOL 1107
BIOL 1108.rationale: Experiments explicitly address evolution, cells, genetics, energy and physiology accompanying BIOL 1107.

BIOL 1111.guard: seen through the lens of evolutionary theory
BIOL 1111.name: General Biology 1
BIOL 1111.rationale: Cell anatomy/physiology, reproduction, heredity and protein synthesis establish biological science; societal examples contextualize those biological concepts.

BIOL 1112.name: Lab for BIOL 1111
BIOL 1112.rationale: Experimental and simulation work accompanies BIOL 1111 biology; statistical analysis and writing are supporting lab practices.

BIOL 1113.guard: ecological relationships at the population, community, and ecosystem levels
BIOL 1113.name: General Biology 2
BIOL 1113.rationale: Organismal diversity, integrative biology and ecological relationships are substantive biological-science content.

BIOL 1114.name: Lab for BIOL 1113
BIOL 1114.rationale: Experiments accompany BIOL 1113 organismal and ecological biology.

BIOL 1141.name: Microbes and Society
BIOL 1141.rationale: Microorganism growth and behavior are studied through food, health, waste management and biogeochemical applications; the primary subject is microbiology.

BIOL 1143.name: Biology and Society
BIOL 1143.rationale: The description teaches biological mechanisms of inheritance, energy, evolution and population dynamics as a framework for interpreting public issues; the primary content remains biological principles.

BIOL 1147.guard: structure and function of the human body
BIOL 1147.name: The Human Organism
BIOL 1147.rationale: Human body structure and function in health and disease are anatomy/physiology domain knowledge.

BIOL 2217.guard: structure and function of cells and tissues
BIOL 2217.name: Integrated Anatomy and Physiology 1
BIOL 2217.rationale: Human cells, tissues, skin, bones, muscles, blood and nervous-system function establish anatomy and physiology.

BIOL 2218.name: Lab for BIOL 2217
BIOL 2218.rationale: Experiments accompany the specific human anatomy and physiology of BIOL 2217.

BIOL 2299.name: Inquiries in Biological Sciences
BIOL 2299.rationale: Readings, discussion and projects explicitly deepen fundamental biological principles and current biological scientific practice.

BIOL 2301.name: Genetics and Molecular Biology
BIOL 2301.rationale: Inheritance, gene/genome function, developmental genetics and molecular biological methods are substantive biological science; computational tools are part of this domain work.

BIOL 2302.guard: scientific investigation methods and data analysis
BIOL 2302.name: Lab for BIOL 2301
BIOL 2302.rationale: The laboratory investigates and analyzes genetics/molecular biology from BIOL 2301.

BIOL 2309.name: Biology Project Lab
BIOL 2309.rationale: Independent projects use explicitly specified cell and molecular biology approaches and techniques, providing a substantive domain unlike an unspecified research topic.

BIOL 2327.guard: life cycles, modes of transmission, and pathogenesis
BIOL 2327.name: Human Parasitology
BIOL 2327.rationale: Parasite biology, life cycles, transmission and pathogenesis are biological/health domain content.

BIOL 2329.guard: ethical issues arising from biological research
BIOL 2329.name: Bioethics
BIOL 2329.rationale: The primary stated activity is identifying and critically analyzing ethical implications of biological research and technology, including genome editing and international perspectives.

BIOL 2407.guard: sequence datasets generated by research labs
BIOL 2407.name: Computational Project Lab
BIOL 2407.rationale: Read mapping, expression analysis and phylogenetic workflows apply computation to biological sequence datasets; the description does not establish general software construction or AI as the primary subject.

BIOL 3401.guard: morphology and phylogeny of the vertebrates
BIOL 3401.name: Comparative Vertebrate Anatomy
BIOL 3401.rationale: Vertebrate morphology and phylogeny are explicitly specified biological-science subject matter.

BIOL 3405.name: Neurobiology
BIOL 3405.rationale: Cellular/molecular nervous-system function, neuronal circuits, sensory processing and motor output are neurobiology, not artificial neural-network methods.

BIOL 3413.name: Current Topics in Organismal and Population Biology
BIOL 3413.rationale: Although offerings vary, the description explicitly confines the subject to organismal and population biology; the domain is biological science.

BIOL 3415.name: Current Topics in Behavioral Neuroscience
BIOL 3415.rationale: Although selected topics vary, they are explicitly behavioral neuroscience; this is biological domain content rather than an inferred AI classification.

BIOL 3425.guard: digital technologies differentially impact neurological development
BIOL 3425.name: Developmental Neuroplasticity and Technology
BIOL 3425.rationale: The course investigates neurological development and brain-environment effects of digital technologies through biological research; technology is the exposure being studied, not an AI-method curriculum.

BIOL 3427.name: Microbial Evolution
BIOL 3427.rationale: Microbial origins, metabolism, diversity, evolution and ecological impact establish biological-science content.

BIOL 3451.name: Avian Biology
BIOL 3451.rationale: Bird morphology, physiology, evolution, behavior and ecology, with field observations, are explicitly avian biological science.

BIOL 3601.guard: major experimental approaches and key concepts
BIOL 3601.name: Neural Systems and Behavior
BIOL 3601.rationale: Experimental behavioral neurobiology, sensory/motor systems and cellular learning mechanisms concern biological nervous systems, not machine learning.

BIOL 3605.guard: cellular, molecular, and genetic processes that guide neural development
BIOL 3605.name: Developmental Neurobiology
BIOL 3605.rationale: Cellular, molecular and genetic processes that generate and connect nerve cells are developmental neurobiology.

BIOL 3611.name: Biochemistry
BIOL 3611.rationale: Biomolecular structure/function, bioenergetics, enzymes and metabolic pathways are biochemistry.

BIOL 3612.name: Lab for BIOL 3611
BIOL 3612.rationale: Experiments accompany the explicitly reviewed biomolecular and metabolic content of BIOL 3611.

BIOL 4701.guard: development of an original research proposal
BIOL 4701.name: Biology Capstone
BIOL 4701.rationale: The capstone combines integration of biology experiences, research-proposal development and communication/critique without specifying a narrower dominant course topic; preserve its mixed research-and-communication scope.

BIOL 4705.name: Neurobiology of Cognitive Decline
BIOL 4705.rationale: Brain aging, neuronal damage, neurodegenerative disease, animal models and imaging are substantive neurobiological science.

BIOL 4707.guard: organization and function of eukaryotic cells
BIOL 4707.name: Cell and Molecular Biology
BIOL 4707.rationale: Eukaryotic cell organization, gene expression, signaling, energetics, motility and cell death establish cell/molecular biology.

BIOL 4709.name: Neurobiology of Learning and Memory
BIOL 4709.rationale: Learning and memory are examined through synapses, neural circuits and biological mnemonic mechanisms; these are not artificial learning algorithms.

BIOL 4900.guard: original research under the guidance of an approved mentor
BIOL 4900.name: Biology Research Capstone
BIOL 4900.rationale: The research capstone specifies proposal, reporting and feedback activities around an independently chosen research project; it does not fix that project subject.

BIOL 4970.name: Junior/Senior Honors Project 1
BIOL 4970.rationale: The honors project depends on an individually selected research or production topic; major affiliation does not determine the actual subject.

BIOL 4971.name: Junior/Senior Honors Project 2
BIOL 4971.rationale: The second honors-project semester continues individually selected research or production without a fixed subject in the description.

BIOL 4991.name: Research
BIOL 4991.rationale: The description explicitly says research content depends on the instructor and a chosen topic; do not infer a subject from the department.

BIOL 4994.name: Internship
BIOL 4994.rationale: The description offers internship work without specifying the placement, duties or substantive topic; the category remains unclassified.

BIOL 5581.guard: Topics vary and may include microscopic and macroscopic approaches
BIOL 5581.name: Biological Imaging
BIOL 5581.rationale: Imaging principles and microscopic/macroscopic techniques are explicitly applied to biological problems across cell biology, neuroscience, ecology and biochemistry.

BIOL 5585.name: Evolution
BIOL 5585.rationale: Evolutionary theory, evidence and speciation mechanisms are substantive biological-science content.

BIOL 5591.name: Advanced Genomics
BIOL 5591.rationale: Sequencing, genomic arrays/databases and functional/whole-genome analysis establish genomics domain methods; databases here are biological analytical resources, not a computing-infrastructure curriculum.

BIOL 5595.guard: molecular mechanisms that underlie biological networks
BIOL 5595.name: Cell and Molecular Neuroscience
BIOL 5595.rationale: Molecular neuronal signaling, ion channels, synapses and neurological disease establish cellular/molecular neuroscience, distinct from artificial neural networks.

BIOL 5601.guard: acquisition and control of sensorimotor behavior
BIOL 5601.name: Multidisciplinary Approaches in Motor Control
BIOL 5601.rationale: Human sensorimotor behavior is studied through neurophysiology, imaging and rehabilitation approaches; motor learning here concerns biological motor control.

BNSC 1000.guard: academic support resources and leadership opportunities
BNSC 1000.name: Behavioral Neuroscience at Northeastern
BNSC 1000.rationale: The course introduces university resources, advisors, experiential options and academic success skills; it is orientation rather than a substantive neuroscience survey.

CHEM 1151.name: General Chemistry for Engineers
CHEM 1151.rationale: States of matter, chemical bonding, thermodynamics, equilibrium and electrochemistry are chemical-science domain content.

CHEM 1153.name: Recitation for CHEM 1151
CHEM 1153.rationale: The zero-hour recitation discusses the explicitly reviewed general-chemistry problems and assignments of CHEM 1151.

CHEM 1161.guard: underlying molecular dynamics of living systems
CHEM 1161.name: General Chemistry for Science Majors
CHEM 1161.rationale: Chemical bonding, molecular interactions, kinetics and thermodynamics establish chemical-science content, with living systems as examples.

CHEM 1162.name: Lab for CHEM 1161
CHEM 1162.rationale: The lab teaches chemical laboratory techniques, analysis and chemical/physical processes accompanying CHEM 1161.

CHEM 1163.name: Recitation for CHEM 1161
CHEM 1163.rationale: The zero-hour recitation applies the chemical concepts of the accompanying CHEM 1161 lecture.

CHEM 2161.guard: in the context of modern materials
CHEM 2161.name: Concepts in Chemistry
CHEM 2161.rationale: Thermodynamics, electrochemistry and nuclear, supramolecular and solid-state chemistry are studied through material properties and chemical reactivity.

CHEM 2162.name: Lab for CHEM 2161
CHEM 2162.rationale: Hands-on work in electrochemistry and nuclear, supramolecular and solid-state chemistry makes this chemical laboratory practice.

CHEM 2163.name: Recitation for CHEM 2161
CHEM 2163.rationale: The zero-hour recitation reinforces the explicitly reviewed thermodynamics, electrochemistry and material chemistry of CHEM 2161 through interactive lecture/laboratory problem solving.

CHEM 2311.name: Organic Chemistry 1
CHEM 2311.rationale: Organic structure, stereochemistry, reactions and mechanisms are the specific chemical subject matter.

CHEM 2312.name: Lab for CHEM 2311
CHEM 2312.rationale: Distillation, extraction, chromatography and microscale organic synthesis are chemical laboratory methods.

CHEM 2313.name: Organic Chemistry 2
CHEM 2313.rationale: Organic functional-group chemistry and spectroscopic structural identification continue the organic chemistry sequence.

CHEM 2314.name: Lab for CHEM 2313
CHEM 2314.rationale: Chemical reactions and IR/NMR characterization of organic molecules are laboratory chemistry, not general data analysis or AI.

CHEM 2315.name: Organic Chemistry 1 for Chemistry Majors
CHEM 2315.rationale: Organic bonding, stereochemistry, reaction mechanisms and synthesis establish chemistry as the domain.

CHEM 2316.name: Lab for CHEM 2315
CHEM 2316.rationale: Synthesis, purification and characterization through organic laboratory techniques accompany CHEM 2315.

CHEM 2317.guard: multistep syntheses using the retrosynthesis approach
CHEM 2317.name: Organic Chemistry 2 for Chemistry Majors
CHEM 2317.rationale: Structure-reactivity relationships, spectroscopy, retrosynthesis and organic reaction mechanisms are chemical science.

CHEM 2318.guard: characterization of products from microscale syntheses
CHEM 2318.name: Lab for CHEM 2317
CHEM 2318.rationale: IR/NMR characterization of products from microscale syntheses is organic chemistry laboratory practice.

CHEM 2321.guard: quantitative understanding of homogeneous and heterogeneous equilibria
CHEM 2321.name: Analytical Chemistry
CHEM 2321.rationale: Quantitative equilibria, titrations, separations, spectroscopy and electrochemistry are analytical chemistry; statistics is a supporting method rather than the sole subject.

CHEM 2322.guard: hands-on experience in the analytical methods
CHEM 2322.name: Lab for CHEM 2321
CHEM 2322.rationale: Gravimetry, titrations, spectroscopy, voltammetry and chromatography are explicitly named analytical chemistry experiments.

CHEM 2323.name: Recitation for CHEM 2321
CHEM 2323.rationale: The zero-hour recitation reinforces the explicitly reviewed analytical chemistry of CHEM 2321 through interactive lecture/laboratory problem solving.

CHEM 2324.name: Recitation for CHEM 2315
CHEM 2324.rationale: The zero-hour recitation reinforces the explicitly reviewed organic chemistry and synthesis of CHEM 2315 through interactive lecture/laboratory problem solving.

CHEM 2325.name: Recitation for CHEM 2317
CHEM 2325.rationale: The zero-hour recitation reinforces the explicitly reviewed organic reactivity and spectroscopy of CHEM 2317 through interactive lecture/laboratory problem solving.

CHEM 3331.name: Bioanalytical Chemistry
CHEM 3331.rationale: Biomolecular analysis, sequencing, biosensors and bioassays are bioanalytical chemistry techniques, not an unspecified computing course.

CHEM 3332.name: Lab for CHEM 3331
CHEM 3332.rationale: The laboratory applies analytical instrumentation to biotechnology and pharmaceutical research contexts.

CHEM 3401.name: Chemical Thermodynamics and Kinetics
CHEM 3401.rationale: Thermodynamic laws are applied to chemical reactions, phase equilibria and physical chemical measurements; this is chemical-science domain content.

CHEM 3402.guard: experimental protocol and methods of data analysis
CHEM 3402.name: Lab for CHEM 3401
CHEM 3402.rationale: Experiments measure gas behavior, electrochemical equilibrium, phase diagrams and calorimetry accompanying CHEM 3401.

CHEM 3410.guard: geochemical principles that shape the natural and managed environment
CHEM 3410.name: Environmental Geochemistry
CHEM 3410.rationale: Elemental cycles, minerals and atmospheric/terrestrial/aquatic geochemistry establish environmental chemical-science content.

CHEM 4750.name: Senior Research
CHEM 4750.rationale: The description specifies individually directed experimental research but no fixed research topic. Department membership and prerequisites do not establish the selected project subject.

CHEM 5620.name: Protein Chemistry
CHEM 5620.rationale: Protein properties, synthesis, structure, folding, purification and biophysical characterization are molecular chemical-science content.

CHME 2308.name: Conservation Principles in Chemical Engineering
CHME 2308.rationale: Mass/energy balance and chemical-process analysis are chemical-engineering domain practice, not mathematical theory merely because calculations are used.

CHME 2310.name: Transport Processes 1
CHME 2310.rationale: The primary subject is physical fluid and energy transport in engineering processes; mathematical methods serve that domain.

CHME 2320.guard: first and second laws of thermodynamics
CHME 2320.name: Engineering Thermodynamics
CHME 2320.rationale: Thermodynamic laws, properties and engineering systems are physical/engineering domain knowledge.

CHME 3305.name: Chemical Engineering Laboratory
CHME 3305.rationale: The course is a chemical-engineering laboratory centered on transport experiments and design; communication supports the domain practice.

CHME 3306.name: Recitation for CHME 3305
CHME 3306.rationale: The explicit accompanying CHME 3305 laboratory context establishes engineering experimental practice; zero hours do not erase the separate required recitation identity.

CHME 3312.name: Transport Processes 2
CHME 3312.rationale: Physical transport phenomena in industrial engineering processes are the substantive domain.

CHME 3322.name: Chemical Thermodynamics
CHME 3322.rationale: Chemical mixture thermodynamics and reaction equilibria are scientific/engineering domain content.

CHME 4510.guard: design of batch and continuous-flow chemical reactors
CHME 4510.name: Chemical Engineering Kinetics
CHME 4510.rationale: Reaction rates and reactor design establish chemical-engineering practice; data analysis is a supporting method.

CHME 4512.guard: modeling liquid-level, temperature, and composition dynamics
CHME 4512.name: Chemical Engineering Process Control
CHME 4512.rationale: The description applies transforms, dynamic models and controller design to chemical-process variables. Control systems here are engineering domain content, not computing infrastructure or AI by name.

CHME 4701.name: Separations and Process Analysis
CHME 4701.rationale: Chemical process/separation design, operations and engineering economics are the domain; simulation use does not establish general software construction.

CHME 4703.name: Chemical Process Design Capstone
CHME 4703.rationale: The required capstone designs a chemical process and demonstrates feasibility; ethical/economic constraints and reports support the engineering design objective.

CHME 4705.name: Recitation for CHME 4703
CHME 4705.rationale: The source explicitly accompanies the chemical-process design capstone; its domain classification is based on that named course relationship rather than its recitation title alone.

CRIM 1000.name: Criminal Justice at Northeastern
CRIM 1000.rationale: The stated content is university orientation, study skills, services and career awareness rather than a substantive criminological method.

CRIM 1100.name: Introduction to Criminal Justice
CRIM 1100.rationale: The course analyzes criminal-justice institutions, actors, policies and systemic inequalities in the United States.

CRIM 1110.guard: arrests, searches and seizures, right to counsel
CRIM 1110.name: Criminal Due Process
CRIM 1110.rationale: Constitutional rights, criminal procedure and legal interpretation are the stated subject.

CRIM 1120.guard: measurement issues in the field of criminology
CRIM 1120.name: Criminology
CRIM 1120.rationale: The course develops criminological theories, crime causation and social responses with explicit attention to inequalities and bias.

CRIM 1300.name: The Death Penalty
CRIM 1300.rationale: Capital punishment is studied through history, constitutional decisions, public controversies and social inequalities.

CRIM 1400.guard: experiences and needs of trafficking victims
CRIM 1400.name: Human Trafficking
CRIM 1400.rationale: Human trafficking is examined through victims, networks and the social and cultural practices that enable exploitation.

CRIM 1500.guard: measure corruption, governance, and anticorruption efforts
CRIM 1500.name: Corruption, Integrity, and Accountability
CRIM 1500.rationale: Corruption, governance, legal standards, accountability and ethics are the primary content; measurement examples do not make this a mathematical-method course.

CRIM 1700.name: Crime, Media, and Politics
CRIM 1700.rationale: The course critiques political and media representations of crime and justice through historical and social analysis.

CRIM 2310.guard: separation of powers and of judicial review
CRIM 2310.name: Courts: The Third Branch of Government
CRIM 2310.rationale: Judicial organization, constitutional foundations and relations among government branches are the subject.

CRIM 2320.guard: prevention and diversion to institutional corrections
CRIM 2320.name: Youth Crime and Justice
CRIM 2320.rationale: Juvenile justice policy, institutions, philosophies and inequities are analyzed in their social context.

CRIM 2330.name: Punishment in the Age of Mass Incarceration
CRIM 2330.rationale: The course examines punishment, sentencing and correctional institutions historically and in contemporary policy.

CRIM 2350.name: Policing a Democratic Society
CRIM 2350.rationale: Policing is analyzed as a social institution, including organizational culture, accountability, history and research.

CRIM 2370.name: Restorative Justice: Transforming the System
CRIM 2370.rationale: Restorative justice and penal institutions are examined using critical race and social systems theories; systems does not refer to computing infrastructure.

CRIM 2380.guard: social and psychological harms of incarceration
CRIM 2380.name: Black Families and Incarceration
CRIM 2380.rationale: The course studies Black families in carceral institutions through historical, cultural and policy analysis.

CRIM 3010.name: Criminal Violence
CRIM 3010.rationale: The course examines causes, social patterns and criminal-justice responses to violence, integrating sociological and psychological perspectives.

CRIM 3030.name: Global Criminology
CRIM 3030.rationale: Cross-national definitions and responses to crime are studied in cultural and institutional context.

CRIM 3040.guard: cognitive, emotional, perceptual, and physiological phenomena
CRIM 3040.name: Psychology of Crime
CRIM 3040.rationale: The primary focus is offenders cognitive, emotional, perceptual and physiological processes and their development, applied to prevention and desistance; this is psychological domain study.

CRIM 3050.guard: interconnections between organized criminals and legitimate organizations
CRIM 3050.name: Organized Crime
CRIM 3050.rationale: Criminal enterprises and organized crime are examined through social, economic, political and legislative relationships.

CRIM 3060.guard: prevention efforts designed to combat political crime and terrorism
CRIM 3060.name: Political Crime and Terrorism
CRIM 3060.rationale: Political crime and terrorism are studied historically and through contemporary prevention policies and information sources.

CRIM 3070.guard: criminal justice and regulatory justice systems
CRIM 3070.name: Corporate and White-Collar Crime
CRIM 3070.rationale: Corporate offending is examined through criminal and regulatory institutions, definitions, case studies and causes.

CRIM 3100.guard: application of legal principles to fact situations
CRIM 3100.name: Criminal Law
CRIM 3100.rationale: Criminal law, legal responsibility and constitutional, moral and public-policy reasoning are the core content.

CRIM 3110.name: Gender, Crime, and Justice
CRIM 3110.rationale: Gender and criminological theory are applied to offending, victimization and justice-system professions.

CRIM 3120.name: Race, Crime, and Justice
CRIM 3120.rationale: The course analyzes historical and theoretical relationships between race, offending and criminal-justice institutions.

CRIM 3540.name: Substance Use and Social Justice
CRIM 3540.rationale: The description combines social-justice and oppression analysis with biological/psychological determinants and clinical prevention/treatment methods; it does not establish one dominant taxonomy subject.

CRIM 3600.name: Criminal Justice Research Methods
CRIM 3600.rationale: The course teaches social-research questions, designs, critique and implementation for crime and justice, rather than a specified statistical or software-method curriculum.

CRIM 3700.name: Analyzing and Using Data on Crime and Justice
CRIM 3700.rationale: The stated foundation is statistical techniques for social-science questions, quantitative evidence and visualization; crime datasets are the application context.

CRIM 4040.guard: assessing effectiveness of prevention programs and policies
CRIM 4040.name: Crime Prevention
CRIM 4040.rationale: Crime-prevention theories and policies are evaluated at individual and community levels using criminological research.

CRIM 4949.name: Senior Capstone Seminar
CRIM 4949.rationale: The capstone explicitly researches a crime/justice-system problem and proposes a policy solution grounded in institutions, law and criminological evidence; its subject is more specific than unspecified research.

CS 1200.name: First Year Seminar
CS 1200.rationale: University transition, resource use and personal planning fall outside the subject-matter categories; no programming content is established.

CS 1210.name: Professional Development for Khoury Co-op
CS 1210.rationale: Co-op preparation, resumes, interviews and workplace conduct do not establish a primary computing subject category.

CS 1800.name: Discrete Structures
CS 1800.rationale: Sets, relations, induction, proof, logic and counting form discrete mathematical methods; computing motivates their use.

CS 1802.name: Seminar for CS 1800
CS 1802.rationale: The seminar accompanies the explicitly reviewed discrete-structures course and reinforces its mathematical topics through discussion and assignments.

CS 2000.name: Introduction to Program Design and Implementation
CS 2000.rationale: The course teaches program construction, coding and introductory data processing to students without programming experience.

CS 2001.name: Lab for CS 2000
CS 2001.rationale: The lab explicitly accompanies the introductory program-design course and practices its computing topics.

CS 2100.guard: fundamentals of program design and implementation
CS 2100.name: Program Design and Implementation 1
CS 2100.rationale: Data/object-oriented design, data structures, abstraction, testing and software construction are the central methods.

CS 2101.name: Lab for CS 2100
CS 2101.rationale: The lab explicitly accompanies the reviewed program-design and software-construction course.

CS 2484.guard: designing, prototyping, and evaluating user interfaces
CS 2484.name: Principles of Human-Computer Interaction
CS 2484.rationale: Human-centered interface design, prototyping and usability evaluation constitute applied interaction-design practice, rather than general programming or an AI method.

CS 3200.name: Introduction to Databases
CS 3200.rationale: Relational database design, query processing, indexing, concurrency and recovery are database-system methods.

CS 4100.guard: algorithms of the artificial intelligence field
CS 4100.name: Principles of Artificial Intelligence
CS 4100.rationale: The description explicitly teaches AI representations, search, decision-making under uncertainty and learning algorithms.

CS 4120.name: Natural Language Processing
CS 4120.rationale: Computational grammar, statistical language models, semantic interpretation and intelligent language agents form the NLP subfield of AI.

CS 4520.guard: project that produces a professional-quality mobile application
CS 4520.name: Mobile Application Development
CS 4520.rationale: The central task is software construction for mobile platforms, integrating interfaces, data handling and networking into an application.

CS 4991.name: Research
CS 4991.rationale: The description provides supervised research but no fixed research topic; prerequisite courses do not determine its subject classification.

CY 4170.name: The Law, Ethics, and Policy of Data and Digital Technologies
CY 4170.rationale: The description centers on legal rights, data ethics, privacy and the social impact of information practices, not security implementation.

CY 5240.guard: legal infrastructure relating to information assurance
CY 5240.name: Cyberlaw: Privacy, Ethics, and Digital Rights
CY 5240.rationale: The course studies law, privacy, rights and criminal misuse surrounding information security rather than technical security mechanisms.

DEAF 2700.guard: structural properties of American Sign Language
DEAF 2700.name: ASL Linguistics
DEAF 2700.rationale: The description primarily examines ASL phonological, morphological, semantic and syntactic structure; sociolinguistic variation supports this specific linguistic-domain study.

DS 1300.guard: normative frameworks from epistemology and ethics
DS 1300.name: Knowledge in a Digital World
DS 1300.rationale: Ethics and epistemology evaluate the societal effects of information technologies and policies; technology examples do not make this an AI-methods course.

DS 3000.name: Mathematical Foundations of Artificial Intelligence
DS 3000.rationale: The description explicitly emphasizes linear algebra, probability and numerical mathematical foundations, using AI as their motivating application.

DS 3500.guard: design and implementation of enterprise-grade software systems
DS 3500.name: Advanced Programming with Data
DS 3500.rationale: Software architectures, reusable APIs, testing and maintainable data pipelines center on general software design and implementation.

DS 4200.name: Information Presentation and Visualization
DS 4200.rationale: Visualization combines programming, perception, visual communication and domain presentation; the description does not establish one defensible primary category among these.

DS 4300.name: Large-Scale Information Storage and Retrieval
DS 4300.rationale: Distributed databases, storage architectures, reliability and data retrieval are computing infrastructure methods.

DS 4400.name: Machine Learning
DS 4400.rationale: Supervised and unsupervised learning, predictive models, model evaluation and learning algorithms are the explicit central content.

DS 4420.guard: advanced supervised and unsupervised machine learning concepts
DS 4420.name: Advanced Machine Learning
DS 4420.rationale: Advanced learning algorithms, structured-data models, Bayesian estimation and generative models are explicitly machine-learning content.

DS 4440.name: Modern Neural Networks
DS 4440.rationale: Neural-network optimization, architectures and deep-learning tools are the central methods.

ECON 1000.name: Economics at Northeastern
ECON 1000.rationale: First-year academic orientation, interpersonal skills and university community are not mathematical methods or a fixed economics-content course.

ECON 1115.name: Principles of Macroeconomics
ECON 1115.rationale: Macroeconomic institutions, policy, unemployment, inflation and inequality constitute social/economic analysis.

ECON 1116.guard: interaction of consumers, firms, and governments
ECON 1116.name: Principles of Microeconomics
ECON 1116.rationale: The focus is interaction of consumers, firms and governments and the social consequences of markets, efficiency and equity.

ECON 1292.name: Economic History of the Middle East
ECON 1292.rationale: The source describes historical economies, political institutions, law, commerce and regional relations.

ECON 2315.guard: impact of various macroeconomic policy tools
ECON 2315.name: Macroeconomic Theory
ECON 2315.rationale: Mathematical tools analyze employment, prices, growth, policy and social justice; the primary object is macroeconomic behavior rather than mathematical theory.

ECON 2316.guard: welfare and distributional impacts of policies
ECON 2316.name: Microeconomic Theory
ECON 2316.rationale: Calculus supports analysis of consumers, firms, market failures and policy welfare effects; this is economic/social analysis, not a calculus course.

ECON 2350.guard: confidence interval estimation, hypothesis testing, and simple regression analysis
ECON 2350.name: Statistics for Economists
ECON 2350.rationale: Sampling, estimation, hypothesis tests and regression are statistical methods, with economics providing the data context.

ECON 2560.name: Applied Econometrics
ECON 2560.rationale: Multivariate regression, specification, inference and econometric model techniques constitute statistical methodology.

ECON 3290.name: History of the Global Economy
ECON 3290.rationale: Historical inequality, trade regimes, debt and competing economic systems are the primary subject.

ECON 3291.guard: major policy issues concerning health, education
ECON 3291.name: Development Economics
ECON 3291.rationale: The course assesses development, poverty, inequality and social policy using empirical economic tools; it is not a course primarily in statistical theory.

ECON 3404.guard: economic and political dimensions of food policy
ECON 3404.name: International Food Policy
ECON 3404.rationale: Food policy, poverty, governance and institutions are studied as social/economic systems.

ECON 3405.guard: origins, workings, successes, and failures of capitalism
ECON 3405.name: A Critique of Capitalism
ECON 3405.rationale: The course critically compares capitalist and alternative social/economic arrangements.

ECON 3413.guard: goal of answering health policy questions
ECON 3413.name: Health Economics and Healthcare Policy
ECON 3413.rationale: Economic models and data serve analysis of insurance, provider behavior, affordability and health-policy debates.

ECON 3423.guard: taxation, regulations, marketable permits, and property rights
ECON 3423.name: Environmental Economics
ECON 3423.rationale: Environmental externalities, property rights and regulatory policy are analyzed economically; the source does not primarily teach mathematical theory.

ECON 3424.name: Law and Economics
ECON 3424.rationale: Legal rules, incentives, social welfare and the development of common law are the central analytical objects.

ECON 3635.name: International Economics
ECON 3635.rationale: Trade policy, monetary institutions and international economic arrangements are the central content.

ECON 4692.guard: problems of personal and philosophical significance
ECON 4692.name: Senior Economics Seminar
ECON 4692.rationale: The seminar applies economics to individually chosen issues; the public description does not establish a single fixed topic for the subject taxonomy.

ECON 4997.guard: research project on a topic within the discipline of economics
ECON 4997.name: Senior Economics Thesis
ECON 4997.rationale: The economics thesis topic and method are student-defined; a prerequisite list does not establish its primary subject category.

ECON 5650.guard: sources of income and growth differences across countries
ECON 5650.name: Economic Growth and Applications
ECON 5650.rationale: Growth models explain differences among economies, institutions, technology and inequality; the object is economic/social analysis.

EEAM 2000.name: Professional Development for Co-op
EEAM 2000.rationale: The course prepares students for co-op searches, professional behavior and career choices rather than a substantive discipline-method curriculum.

EECE 2160.name: Embedded Design: Enabling Robotics
EECE 2160.rationale: The description integrates digital hardware design, object-oriented programming/Linux and a robotic-device project without establishing one dominant subject among systems, programming and domain implementation. The robotics example does not establish an AI-method course.

EECE 2322.name: Fundamentals of Digital Design and Computer Organization
EECE 2322.rationale: Logic circuits, instruction-set architecture, processor construction, hardware-description languages and assembly interfaces establish computer architecture/digital systems as the primary subject.

EECE 2323.name: Lab for EECE 2322
EECE 2323.rationale: The laboratory designs, implements, simulates and tests a computer system on programmable logic using a hardware-description language.

EEMB 1101.guard: designing and implementing independent field research
EEMB 1101.name: Foundations in Ecology and Evolutionary Biology
EEMB 1101.rationale: Ecological adaptation, evolution and ecosystem study supply the biological domain; field research is a method for investigating that domain.

EEMB 1102.name: Lab for EEMB 1101
EEMB 1102.rationale: The laboratory explicitly accompanies the separately read ecology/evolution lecture and experiments on its biological topics.

EEMB 1105.name: Foundations in Ecological and Evolutionary Genomics
EEMB 1105.rationale: Sequencing and command-line skills serve questions in molecular ecology and evolutionary genomics; general programming is not the primary subject.

EEMB 1106.name: Lab for EEMB 1105
EEMB 1106.rationale: Laboratory tools test ecological and evolutionary hypotheses, establishing a biological experimental domain.

EEMB 2302.name: Ecology
EEMB 2302.rationale: Environmental/biological controls on species distribution and abundance, ecological experiments and scientific evidence establish ecology-domain content; quantitative attributes do not alone make it mathematics.

EEMB 2303.name: Lab for EEMB 2302
EEMB 2303.rationale: The laboratory expressly accompanies ecological principles and experiments in EEMB2302; its substantive domain is ecology rather than generic data analysis.

EEMB 2400.name: Introduction to Evolution
EEMB 2400.rationale: Evolutionary mechanisms, adaptation, speciation and biological history integrate genetic and ecological evidence as biological domain science.

EEMB 2610.name: Plant Biology
EEMB 2610.rationale: Plant anatomy, physiology, evolution and ecology establish substantive biological knowledge.

EEMB 2700.guard: biological aspects of natural ocean ecosystems
EEMB 2700.name: Marine Biology
EEMB 2700.rationale: Marine organism interactions, physiology, energy and ecosystem processes are biological/ocean-domain science; proposal writing supports the scientific work.

EEMB 2701.name: Lab for EEMB 2700
EEMB 2701.rationale: The laboratory applies the marine-biological topics of EEMB2700 through experiments and discussion.

EEMB 3455.name: Ecosystems Ecology
EEMB 3455.rationale: Energy and elemental flows through ecosystems are environmental and biological subject matter, despite quantitative analysis.

EEMB 3460.guard: causes and consequences of biodiversity loss
EEMB 3460.name: Conservation Biology
EEMB 3460.rationale: Ecological/evolutionary principles are applied to biodiversity loss and conservation problems; sustainability and societal context do not erase the biological conservation focus.

EEMB 3465.guard: genetic diversity at the individual to population level
EEMB 3465.name: Ecological and Conservation Genomics
EEMB 3465.rationale: Population genetics and conservation problems organize the R exercises and mathematical derivations; the course primarily teaches a biological domain.

EEMB 3466.name: Disease Ecology
EEMB 3466.rationale: Host-pathogen ecology and evolution integrate physiological effects, empirical disease studies and ecological systems. Mathematical models support this domain investigation rather than constitute a general mathematics course.

EEMB 3475.name: Wildlife Ecology
EEMB 3475.rationale: Wildlife management, habitats, populations and conservation are the substantive domain; basic models support it.

EEMB 3600.name: Animal Behavior
EEMB 3600.rationale: Physiological, ecological and genetic explanations of evolved animal behavior are biological-domain knowledge, not artificial learning systems.

EEMB 4001.guard: look at and interpret spatial data
EEMB 4001.name: Landscape and Restoration Ecology
EEMB 4001.rationale: Landscape processes, disturbances, habitats and restoration establish ecological domain study, with spatial data as a tool.

EEMB 5130.name: Population Dynamics
EEMB 5130.rationale: The description foregrounds derivation, dynamical analysis, stability, optimization and model validation; population examples organize a course centered on mathematical modeling tools.

EESC 2000.name: Professional Development for Co-op
EESC 2000.rationale: The course teaches co-op procedures, job search, professional behavior and career decisions; it does not establish a disciplinary scientific curriculum.

EESH 2000.name: Professional Development for Co-op
EESH 2000.rationale: The course develops co-op job-search, résumé, interviewing and career-management skills; professional preparation does not establish one of the substantive subject categories.

ENCP 2000.guard: job search and career management skills
ENCP 2000.name: Introduction to Engineering Co-op Education
ENCP 2000.rationale: The description centers on employment searches, career management and co-op procedures, without a fixed substantive engineering curriculum.

ENCP 3000.name: Professional Issues in Engineering
ENCP 3000.rationale: Professional ethics, ethical conflicts, diversity and cultural context are explicit substantive topics, distinguishing this course from generic employment-search preparation.

ENGW 1102.name: First-Year Writing for Multilingual Writers
ENGW 1102.rationale: The description teaches writing, rhetorical choices and communication across audiences and genres, with support for multilingual writers; it is not programming.

ENGW 1111.name: First-Year Writing
ENGW 1111.rationale: The workshop teaches rhetorical choices, research-based writing, audience awareness and revision in academic, professional and public communication.

ENGW 1114.guard: writing projects meet specific community needs
ENGW 1114.name: First-Year Writing with Service-Learning
ENGW 1114.rationale: The course applies rhetorical writing and source research to community communication needs through service learning.

ENGW 3302.guard: relevant to technical professions and individual student goals
ENGW 3302.name: Advanced Writing in the Technical Professions
ENGW 3302.rationale: Technical reports, proposals and presentations are the genres used to teach audience analysis, critical research and revision; the subject is technical communication rather than engineering methods.

ENGW 3303.name: Advanced Writing in the Environmental Professions
ENGW 3303.rationale: Environmental concerns supply the context for instruction in analytic reports, audience analysis, source evaluation and written communication.

ENGW 3304.name: Advanced Writing in the Business Administration Professions
ENGW 3304.rationale: Business proposals, recommendation reports and correspondence are used to teach professional writing, audience analysis and revision; business context does not make this a quantitative methods course.

ENGW 3306.name: Advanced Writing in the Health Professions
ENGW 3306.rationale: Health-profession literature reviews, protocols and care instructions are writing genres for audience analysis and critical communication, rather than instruction in clinical procedures.

ENGW 3307.guard: quantitative data and visual presentation of evidence
ENGW 3307.name: Advanced Writing in the Sciences
ENGW 3307.rationale: The course analyzes how scientific texts present claims and evidence and teaches scientific writing and revision; quantitative evidence is a communication object, not the primary mathematical subject.

ENGW 3308.name: Advanced Writing in the Social Sciences
ENGW 3308.rationale: The course teaches social-science writing, argument, presentation of evidence and ethical communication concerning human subjects.

ENGW 3309.name: Advanced Writing in the Humanities
ENGW 3309.rationale: The course teaches interpretation, textual evidence and rhetorical writing in humanities research.

ENGW 3314.name: Advanced Writing in the Arts, Media, and Design
ENGW 3314.rationale: The description emphasizes public and professional writing, critical reviews and multiple literacies in arts, media and design.

ENGW 3315.name: Interdisciplinary Advanced Writing in the Disciplines
ENGW 3315.rationale: Interdisciplinary professional, public and academic writing is taught through audience analysis, critical research, peer review and revision.

ENVR 1110.name: Global Climate Change
ENVR 1110.rationale: Physical climate systems, their history and future change establish environmental science, including adaptation applications.

ENVR 1200.name: Dynamic Earth
ENVR 1200.rationale: Rock processes, landscapes and plate tectonics establish geology as the substantive domain.

ENVR 1201.name: Lab for ENVR 1200
ENVR 1201.rationale: Rock/mineral identification and geological map interpretation are practical geology methods.

ENVR 1400.name: Foundations in Environmental and Sustainability Sciences
ENVR 1400.rationale: The source explicitly integrates physical/ecological science with cultural, political, ethical and economic dimensions; neither side has a clearly dominant separate subject.

ENVR 1401.guard: interface of human and natural systems
ENVR 1401.name: Lab for ENVR 1400
ENVR 1401.rationale: The lab explicitly addresses the human/natural interface and accompanies the separately read integrative environmental-science course; its topic cannot be reduced to natural science alone.

ENVR 2200.name: Earth's Changing Cycles
ENVR 2200.rationale: Biological, chemical and physical Earth cycles and human disturbances establish environmental science.

ENVR 2310.guard: physical and chemical characteristics of common rock-forming minerals
ENVR 2310.name: Earth Materials
ENVR 2310.rationale: Minerals, soils, rocks and formation processes are geological domain content; a writing-intensive designation does not change the subject.

ENVR 2311.name: Lab for ENVR 2310
ENVR 2311.rationale: The experimental lab explicitly accompanies the separately read Earth-materials lecture, establishing geological practice.

ENVR 2340.guard: origin and evolution of landscape features
ENVR 2340.name: Earth Landforms and Processes
ENVR 2340.rationale: Landscape origins and surface processes organize the use of imagery and elevation data, establishing geomorphology.

ENVR 2341.name: Lab for ENVR 2340
ENVR 2341.rationale: The experimental lab accompanies the separately read landforms/processes course; it is geological practice.

ENVR 2500.name: Biostatistics
ENVR 2500.rationale: The source explicitly centers mathematical foundations of statistics, probability, inference, estimation and parametric/nonparametric tests. Biological data provide the application context, not a different primary subject.

ENVR 2501.guard: addressed in the R programming environment
ENVR 2501.name: Lab for ENVR 2500
ENVR 2501.rationale: The laboratory accompanies the explicitly statistical ENVR 2500 and applies its statistical topics in R; using a programming environment does not make the primary subject general software construction.

ENVR 2502.guard: knowledge acquired in lecture and lab
ENVR 2502.name: Recitation for ENVR 2500
ENVR 2502.rationale: The recitation explicitly accompanies ENVR 2500/2501 and practices the statistical knowledge of that lecture/lab. It is a zero-hour statistical-methods course, not missing credit or a programming elective.

ENVR 2515.guard: economic development, social inclusion, and environmental stewardship
ENVR 2515.name: Sustainable Development
ENVR 2515.rationale: The course examines development, social inclusion, economic growth and collective responses to global challenges through critical discussion and projects.

ENVR 3125.guard: physical, biological, and chemical properties of the ocean
ENVR 3125.name: Global Oceanic Change
ENVR 3125.rationale: Physical, biological and chemical ocean changes organize the course; social and political implications supplement the ocean-science domain.

ENVR 3150.name: Food Security and Sustainability
ENVR 3150.rationale: The scientific lens on agriculture, fisheries, aquaculture, nutrition and food production establishes applied food/environmental science.

ENVR 3200.guard: water’s availability and behavior at the Earth’s surface
ENVR 3200.name: Water Resources
ENVR 3200.rationale: Hydrology, water quality and surface/groundwater systems establish water-resource domain knowledge, with regulation and conflicts in context.

ENVR 3300.name: Geographic Information Systems
ENVR 3300.rationale: The description centers on practical geospatial data collection, cartography and GIS analysis across cases; it does not teach general software construction or computing infrastructure.

ENVR 3301.name: Lab for ENVR 3300
ENVR 3301.rationale: The lab accompanies the separately read practical GIS course, supporting applied geospatial methods.

ENVR 3600.guard: processes operating in the world's oceans
ENVR 3600.name: Oceanography
ENVR 3600.rationale: Integrated biological, chemical, physical and geological ocean processes establish oceanography.

ENVR 3800.name: Plants and Society
ENVR 3800.rationale: Plant biology, management and practical uses organize the course, with cultural perspectives in support of the botanical domain.

ENVR 3801.name: Lab for ENVR 3800
ENVR 3801.rationale: Plant identification, physiology and care techniques are applied botanical practice.

ENVR 4050.guard: solve environmental problems that are of concern to various stakeholders
ENVR 4050.name: Solving Emerging Environmental Challenges through Capstone
ENVR 4050.rationale: Projects explicitly solve stakeholder environmental problems using environmental disciplines; communication is supporting professional practice, not evidence of AI content.

ENVR 4500.guard: origin, distribution, and flow of groundwater
ENVR 4500.name: Applied Hydrogeology
ENVR 4500.rationale: Groundwater flow, aquifers, field mapping and remediation establish hydrogeology; mathematical models support domain analysis.

ENVR 4501.name: Lab for ENVR 4500
ENVR 4501.rationale: The lab explicitly accompanies the separately read applied hydrogeology course and experiments on its topics.

ENVR 4505.guard: physical, biological, and cultural aspects of wetlands
ENVR 4505.name: Wetlands
ENVR 4505.rationale: Wetland hydrology, soils, vegetation, ecosystem processes and management provide the dominant environmental domain, alongside societal values.

ENVR 4970.name: Junior/Senior Honors Project 1
ENVR 4970.rationale: The honors project description allows unspecified research or products; a discipline prefix and host degree do not establish the actual project subject.

ENVR 4971.name: Junior/Senior Honors Project 2
ENVR 4971.rationale: Continuation of an unspecified honors research/product project does not establish a defensible subject category.

ENVR 4997.name: Senior Thesis
ENVR 4997.rationale: The source specifies a faculty-supervised undergraduate thesis but does not state its topic or methods.

ENVR 5000.guard: public participation in environmental policy settings
ENVR 5000.name: Community Stakeholder Engagement in Environmental Management and Research
ENVR 5000.rationale: Public participation, deliberation, policy processes and stakeholder engagement are the explicit central subjects.

ENVR 5150.guard: analyzing and interpreting climate data and model output
ENVR 5150.name: Climate and Atmospheric Change
ENVR 5150.rationale: Physical climate change, historical evidence and climate projections establish climate science; using model outputs does not imply an AI or general mathematics course.

ENVR 5190.guard: physical, chemical, and biological properties of soils
ENVR 5190.name: Soil Science
ENVR 5190.rationale: Soil formation, chemistry, biology and management establish soil science.

ENVR 5210.guard: major river and drainage basin processes
ENVR 5210.name: Environmental Planning
ENVR 5210.rationale: Geomorphic and hydrological processes and river/basin calculations anchor environmental planning; regulatory applications remain within that domain practice.

ENVR 5220.guard: principles and practice of ecosystem-based management
ENVR 5220.name: Ecosystem-Based Management
ENVR 5220.rationale: Resource-management approaches, protected areas and habitat restoration establish practical ecosystem management, informed by social and economic principles.

ENVR 5260.guard: input, store, analyze, and display spatial data
ENVR 5260.name: Geographical Information Systems
ENVR 5260.rationale: Geospatial data handling and GIS laboratory practice establish applied geographic analysis; storing data alone is not a systems-course classification.

ENVR 5350.guard: sustainable energy alternatives and emission reduction strategies
ENVR 5350.name: Sustainable Energy and Climate Solutions
ENVR 5350.rationale: Energy sources, emissions and decarbonization strategies establish applied environmental and energy-system knowledge.

ENVR 5450.name: Applied Social-Ecological Systems Modeling
ENVR 5450.rationale: Participatory modeling combines social/ecological research and stakeholder engagement; no specific mathematical-method or natural-science dominance is established.

ENVR 5500.name: Advanced Biostatistics
ENVR 5500.rationale: Statistical foundations, likelihood, model selection, mixed models and multivariate methods organize the course; machine learning is one listed topic within advanced statistics.

ENVR 5563.guard: advanced concepts and techniques in GIS analysis
ENVR 5563.name: Advanced Spatial Analysis
ENVR 5563.rationale: The source combines mathematical spatial objects/statistics, database and information theory, and GIS representation; it does not identify one dominant taxonomy subject.

ENVR 5600.name: Coastal Processes, Adaptation, and Resilience
ENVR 5600.rationale: Coastal forcing, sediment transport, flood hazards and defenses establish physical coastal and adaptation domain practice.

ENVR 5670.guard: interactions between human activity, biogeochemical change, and climate
ENVR 5670.name: Global Biogeochemistry
ENVR 5670.rationale: Global elemental cycles and their biological, physical and chemical interactions establish biogeochemistry.

ENVR 5700.guard: physical, chemical, and biological processes in streams
ENVR 5700.name: Streams and Watershed Ecology
ENVR 5700.rationale: Stream/watershed processes, organisms and field techniques establish ecology, with policy and restoration context.

ENVR 5750.guard: natural systems intersect with human-dominated landscapes
ENVR 5750.name: Urban Ecology
ENVR 5750.rationale: Urban hydrology, nutrient cycles, organisms and ecosystem services establish urban ecology, supplemented by cultural and psychological value.

ENVR 5800.name: Climate Adaptation and Nature-Based Solutions
ENVR 5800.rationale: Ecological resilience, health assessment and nature-based adaptation establish environmental assessment and management practice.

GE 1000.name: First-Year Seminar
GE 1000.rationale: University transition, support resources and major exploration are orientation, not a fixed technical domain.

GE 1110.guard: problem-solving skills used in engineering design
GE 1110.name: Engineering Design
GE 1110.rationale: The description centers on engineering problem formulation, design evaluation, CAD and a technical design project. This is applied engineering design, not an AI method.

GE 1111.guard: structured approach to solve engineering problems
GE 1111.name: Engineering Problem Solving and Computation
GE 1111.rationale: The description uses engineering analysis and design problems to teach computation, matrix tools and microcontrollers. Its primary domain practice is engineering problem solving; it is not evidence of an AI specialization.

GE 1501.name: Cornerstone of Engineering 1
GE 1501.rationale: Hands-on engineering design and prototypes are the organizing domain practice; programming and graphics are supporting tools.

GE 1502.name: Cornerstone of Engineering 2
GE 1502.rationale: The course continues engineering analysis, design, modeling and prototype construction using software and ethical reasoning as tools.

GE 3300.name: Energy Systems: Science, Technology, and Sustainability
GE 3300.rationale: Energy technologies, conversion, end use and sustainability constitute applied energy-engineering knowledge.

HIST 2220.guard: global history of science and technology
HIST 2220.name: History of Technology
HIST 2220.rationale: The course studies the global historical development and circulation of science and technology in society, culture and ethics.

HLTH 1000.name: College: An Introduction
HLTH 1000.rationale: The course introduces university/college resources and academic-social transition skills; it does not establish a substantive clinical or scientific subject curriculum.

HSCI 1000.name: College: An Introduction
HSCI 1000.rationale: Orientation to university, academic skills and learning-community resources does not specify substantive health-science coursework.

HSCI 2000.name: Professional Development for Bouvé Co-op
HSCI 2000.rationale: Job search, interviewing, resumes and co-op procedures constitute career preparation; no narrower disciplinary subject is stated.

INPR 1000.guard: apply design and systems thinking practices
INPR 1000.name: First-Year Interdisciplinary Seminar
INPR 1000.rationale: The first-year seminar emphasizes university resources and personal/academic development with global-challenge context, without a sufficiently specified substantive subject for this taxonomy.

INSC 1000.guard: Introduces first-year students with majors in the College of Science
INSC 1000.name: Science at Northeastern
INSC 1000.rationale: The course introduces college/university resources, academic skills and community transition; a Science host does not establish scientific domain instruction.

INSH 2102.guard: geospatial mapping, data visualization, and network science
INSH 2102.name: Bostonography: The City through Data, Texts, Maps, and Networks
INSH 2102.rationale: Boston geographic, historical, literary, political and civic landscapes are analyzed through computational tools; those tools serve explicit cultural/social questions rather than a general software curriculum.

INSH 3101.name: Research Methods in the Social Sciences
INSH 3101.rationale: The course studies how social research questions, designs and evidence analyze behavior, societal trends, programs and public attitudes; no primary mathematical-method curriculum is stated.

INSH 3102.name: Introduction to Statistics in the Social Sciences
INSH 3102.rationale: The primary subject is statistical techniques and quantitative information for social-science questions, including computation and visualization; the social setting does not replace the stated statistical-method focus.

JRNL 1000.name: Journalism at Northeastern
JRNL 1000.rationale: The description concerns first-year orientation, academic/interpersonal skills and university community values, not substantive journalism methods.

JRNL 1101.name: Journalism 1: Fundamentals of Reporting and Writing
JRNL 1101.rationale: Reporting, newswriting, interviewing, attribution and analysis of media institutions establish communication and social analysis as the subject.

JRNL 1102.guard: photo, audio, video, and data visualization skills
JRNL 1102.name: Journalist’s Toolbox
JRNL 1102.rationale: Photo/audio/video and visualization tools are taught explicitly for journalistic storytelling; operating editing software is not general software construction.

JRNL 1150.guard: media institutions that shape the news
JRNL 1150.name: Understanding Today’s News
JRNL 1150.rationale: The course examines media institutions, press freedom, economics, politics, diversity and news decisions across societies.

JRNL 2201.guard: background research, and use public records
JRNL 2201.name: Journalism 2: Intermediate Reporting
JRNL 2201.rationale: Reporting, interviewing, public-record research and organization of online news stories are the primary communication skills.

JRNL 2301.name: Visual Storytelling in Journalism
JRNL 2301.rationale: The course teaches journalistic storytelling through audio, video and images across presentation formats.

JRNL 3550.guard: libel, invasion of privacy, and access to government information
JRNL 3550.name: The First Amendment and the Media
JRNL 3550.rationale: Libel, privacy, government-information access and competing public/private rights establish legal and ethical analysis.

JRNL 3610.name: Digital Storytelling and Social Media
JRNL 3610.rationale: Digital stories, audience-specific communication and strategic media campaigns are the substantive focus, with technology serving those communication goals.

JRNL 3700.name: Data Storytelling
JRNL 3700.rationale: The course explicitly emphasizes journalistic storytelling for broad public audiences, using quantitative analysis and visualization tools in service of communication.

JRNL 4650.name: Ethics and Diversity in the News Media
JRNL 4650.rationale: News-media responsibilities, professional ethical principles and diversity are examined through current reporting and a major ethical-analysis paper.

JRNL 5500.name: Coding for Digital Storytelling
JRNL 5500.rationale: Unlike storytelling courses that merely use applications, this description explicitly centers on coding and basic web development, Python, JavaScript, APIs and reverse engineering software-based projects.

LING 1150.name: Introduction to Linguistics
LING 1150.rationale: The explicit scientific study of language centers on speech sounds, sound systems, word/sentence structure and meaning; this is linguistic domain knowledge rather than generic writing instruction or AI methods.

LING 2350.guard: semester-long analysis of a world language
LING 2350.name: Linguistic Analysis
LING 2350.rationale: Descriptive analysis of phonetics, phonology, morphology and syntax through a world-language research project establishes linguistic methods; complex datasets alone do not establish programming or statistics.

LING 3412.name: Language and Culture
LING 3412.rationale: The course examines language, culture, social institutions, identity, gender, ethnicity and social class through anthropological/sociolinguistic analysis.

LING 3420.name: Phonetics
LING 3420.rationale: Speech articulation, acoustics and auditory perception are physical/physiological linguistic domain content, consistent with the separate speech-science courses.

LING 3422.guard: patterning of sounds in human language
LING 3422.name: Phonology
LING 3422.rationale: The course studies representations, organization and patterns of human-language sound systems. Formal rules and a quantitative-reasoning attribute do not make the primary subject mathematical theory or AI.

LING 3424.guard: structure, distributional behavior, and use of words
LING 3424.name: Morphology
LING 3424.rationale: Word structure, morphological processes and linguistic theories are the substantive domain; architecture refers to a linguistic theory, not computing infrastructure.

LING 3450.name: Syntax
LING 3450.rationale: The course analyzes sentence structure using linguistic evidence, primarily English syntax; no computational parsing or programming method is stated.

LING 3452.guard: meaning and how it is expressed in language
LING 3452.name: Semantics
LING 3452.rationale: Meaning, sentence structure, intonation and speech acts are analyzed within language science; references to logic, perception and culture serve this linguistic-domain focus.

LING 4654.name: Seminar in Linguistics
LING 4654.rationale: The source specifies a selected current linguistics research topic but no particular content. Linguistics spans structural/scientific and social-cultural subjects, so no narrower taxonomy class is inferred from the department.

LING 4891.guard: group meetings of students and the faculty member
LING 4891.name: Research Seminar in Linguistics
LING 4891.rationale: The research topic, content and requisites are chosen with the instructor; group methods/reporting meetings do not establish a fixed subject classification.

LING 4991.name: Directed Study Research
LING 4991.rationale: Individual research content and requisites depend on the faculty arrangement; no specific substantive topic is supplied.

MATH 1231.name: Calculus for Business and Economics
MATH 1231.rationale: Differentiation, integration and mathematical modeling are the taught methods, applied to business and economics.

MATH 1241.name: Calculus 1
MATH 1241.rationale: The description teaches differentiation and integration, their techniques and mathematical applications.

MATH 1245.guard: differential and integral calculus of one variable
MATH 1245.name: Calculus with Applications
MATH 1245.rationale: Single-variable calculus and introductory differential equations are the central content.

MATH 1340.name: Intensive Calculus for Engineers
MATH 1340.rationale: Precalculus strengthening, differentiation and introductory integration constitute mathematical methods.

MATH 1341.guard: definition, calculation, and major uses of the derivative
MATH 1341.name: Calculus 1 for Science and Engineering
MATH 1341.rationale: Limits, differentiation, integration and the fundamental theorem of calculus are the central content.

MATH 1342.guard: infinite series, and introduction to vectors
MATH 1342.name: Calculus 2 for Science and Engineering
MATH 1342.rationale: Integration techniques, infinite series and vectors are the central mathematical topics.

MATH 1365.name: Introduction to Mathematical Reasoning
MATH 1365.rationale: Mathematical proof, logical argument, sets, relations and functions are explicitly the focus.

MATH 1465.name: Intensive Mathematical Reasoning
MATH 1465.rationale: Proof techniques, sets, cardinality, algebra and group theory provide mathematical reasoning.

MATH 2321.name: Calculus 3 for Science and Engineering
MATH 2321.rationale: Multivariable calculus, vector fields and integration theorems are the taught mathematical methods.

MATH 2331.name: Linear Algebra
MATH 2331.rationale: Vector spaces, linear transformations, spectral theory and decomposition are linear algebra.

MATH 2341.name: Differential Equations and Linear Algebra for Engineering
MATH 2341.rationale: Differential equations, numerical methods, transforms and linear algebra are the taught methods, with engineering applications.

MATH 3081.name: Probability and Statistics
MATH 3081.rationale: Probability distributions, expectation, limit theorems and statistical inference are the core content.

MATH 3082.name: Recitation for MATH 3081
MATH 3082.rationale: The recitation explicitly reinforces the reviewed probability/statistics course.

MATH 3175.name: Group Theory
MATH 3175.rationale: Groups, homomorphisms, cosets and structural group properties are abstract mathematical theory.

MATH 3527.name: Number Theory 1
MATH 3527.rationale: Congruences, modular arithmetic, reciprocity and number-theoretic equations are mathematical theory.

MGSC 2301.guard: sampling and sampling distributions, statistical inference
MGSC 2301.name: Business Statistics
MGSC 2301.rationale: Sampling, inference, hypothesis testing and regression are explicitly the taught statistical methods; business is their application context.

MKTG 4606.name: Digital, Analytics, Technology, and Automation Research Practicum
MKTG 4606.rationale: The practicum centers on solving client business/organizational problems with digital technology and analytics, combining technical and managerial practice. Machine learning is one stated tool, not evidence that a fixed AI algorithm curriculum dominates every project.

PHIL 1000.name: Philosophy at Northeastern
PHIL 1000.rationale: First-year major orientation, university values and academic/interpersonal preparation do not establish a primary disciplinary subject within this taxonomy.

PHIL 1104.guard: analyses of image, text, and ritual
PHIL 1104.name: Goddesses, Witches, Saints, and Sinners: Women and Religion
PHIL 1104.rationale: Historical religious images, texts, rituals and scholarship concerning women and patriarchalization establish cultural and religious analysis.

PHIL 1115.name: Introduction to Logic
PHIL 1115.rationale: Boolean deductive logic and probability calculus for inductive inference explicitly establish formal mathematical and statistical reasoning.

PHIL 1145.guard: ethical issues raised by emerging technologies
PHIL 1145.name: Technology and Human Values
PHIL 1145.rationale: The course studies philosophy and ethics of technology, human relationships with technology and its social dimensions.

PHIL 1165.name: Moral and Social Problems in Healthcare
PHIL 1165.rationale: Ethical theories and principles are applied to moral questions about healthcare, rights, consent, research and resource distribution.

PHIL 1271.name: Sex in Judaism, Christianity, and Islam
PHIL 1271.rationale: Gender, sexuality, marriage and ethical foundations in three religious traditions establish cultural, social and ethical analysis.

PHIL 1300.guard: normative frameworks from epistemology and ethics
PHIL 1300.name: Knowledge in a Digital World
PHIL 1300.rationale: Epistemological and ethical frameworks evaluate information technologies and policies; mentioning machine learning does not establish AI-method instruction.

PHIL 2001.name: Ethics and Evolutionary Games
PHIL 2001.rationale: Evolutionary game theory is introduced to investigate cooperation, fairness, altruism and the origins of ethical/social norms. The stated investigative questions center on those norms; formal modeling is their explanatory tool, not an independently established mathematics-methods focus.

PHIL 2155.name: Human Rights
PHIL 2155.rationale: Political, philosophical and legal dimensions of human rights, their history and contemporary debates establish human/legal context.

PHIL 2325.name: Ancient Philosophy and Political Thought
PHIL 2325.rationale: Classical Greek moral, political and metaphysical writings and written textual analysis establish historical philosophy and political thought.

PHIL 2330.name: Modern Philosophy
PHIL 2330.rationale: Seventeenth- and eighteenth-century philosophical texts are examined in historical, social and political contexts, including underrepresented thinkers.

PHIL 2410.name: Possession, Sacrifice, and Divination in African Diasporic Religions
PHIL 2410.rationale: Comparative religious thought and ritual, slavery and transformations across the African diaspora establish historical and cultural analysis.

PHIL 2619.name: Race and Religion in Film
PHIL 2619.rationale: Film representations of race and religion are analyzed in relation to cultural beliefs, intersecting identities and institutional power.

PHIL 3050.name: Information and Uncertainty
PHIL 3050.rationale: Probabilistic inference, information theory and mathematical methods for uncertain data are the central methods; programming implements those theories rather than defining a general software course.

PHIL 3492.name: Indigenous Philosophy
PHIL 3492.rationale: Indigenous philosophical traditions are studied through ethical, political and cultural questions including sovereignty, locality and decolonization.

PHIL 3512.guard: cultural history, ethnography, and lived religions
PHIL 3512.name: Religion, Race, and Politics
PHIL 3512.rationale: Religion, race and political power are investigated through cultural history, ethnography and changing social structures.

PHIL 3822.name: Philosophy of Race and Racism
PHIL 3822.rationale: Philosophical analysis of race, racism, injustice and intersecting oppression establishes social and ethical subject matter.

PHIL 4050.guard: aligning these impacts with social and ethical values
PHIL 4050.name: Artificial Intelligence and Society
PHIL 4050.rationale: The description examines societal impacts of AI and their alignment with social and ethical values; it does not establish instruction in AI methods.

PHIL 4515.guard: proof systems, decidability, computability, and metatheory
PHIL 4515.name: Advanced Deductive Logic
PHIL 4515.rationale: First-order formal logic, proof systems, decidability, computability and metatheory establish mathematical logic; a computing-related topic alone does not make this software construction.

PHIL 4516.name: Advanced Inductive Logic
PHIL 4516.rationale: Inductive logic, probability, Bayesian updating, confirmation and decision theory establish formal reasoning methods within mathematical logic.

PHIL 5005.name: Information Ethics
PHIL 5005.rationale: Justice, human rights, privacy and the public good govern the treatment of information; information storage terminology does not establish a systems course.

PHIL 5010.name: AI Ethics
PHIL 5010.rationale: The description explicitly takes up philosophical and ethical questions raised by AI, including fairness, responsibility, work and privacy, rather than AI algorithm training.

PHTH 1260.name: The U.S. Healthcare System
PHTH 1260.rationale: The description primarily examines healthcare institutions, organization, financing, access and equity; healthcare systems here are social institutions, not computing infrastructure.

PHTH 1261.name: Comparative Healthcare Systems
PHTH 1261.rationale: The course compares national healthcare delivery, affordability, rights, access, institutions and corporate influences; the primary approach is comparative social/institutional analysis.

PHTH 2210.name: Foundations of Biostatistics
PHTH 2210.rationale: The description centers on biostatistical concepts and statistical thinking applied to health problems; R is a statistical tool rather than a general programming curriculum.

PHTH 2300.name: Communication Skills for the Health Professions
PHTH 2300.rationale: Interpersonal communication, cultural understanding, public speaking and professional presentations are the explicit subject.

PHTH 2301.guard: traditional and new media health communication strategies
PHTH 2301.name: Communication Skills for the Health Professions—Global
PHTH 2301.rationale: Interpersonal, organizational, media and cross-cultural communication methods dominate the description; the health setting does not make these clinical or AI methods.

PHTH 2350.name: Community and Public Health
PHTH 2350.rationale: Population-health improvement, community methods, prevention and management of public-health problems form substantive health-domain practice; social inequality and institutions supply context.

PHTH 2351.name: Community and Public Health - Global
PHTH 2351.rationale: The course applies public-health practices to population disease, environmental and behavioral risks in comparative global settings; social determinants are part of this domain framework.

PHTH 2515.guard: analyze, prepare, and write policy briefs
PHTH 2515.name: Healthcare Policy and Administration
PHTH 2515.rationale: The description centers healthcare policy, institutional management, financing and analysis of economic/legal/political forces, including policy briefs.

PHTH 4120.name: Global Perspectives on Discrimination and Health
PHTH 4120.rationale: The course analyzes discrimination, social categories and population disparities through social/cultural theories, rather than teaching clinical treatment or statistical calculation.

PHTH 4202.name: Principles of Epidemiology in Medicine and Public Health
PHTH 4202.rationale: Epidemiological research-design critique, bias and causal inference in medical/public-health literature are domain research methods. Statistics support interpretation, and the source expressly has no computational requirements; this is not an AI or general statistics course.

PHTH 4540.name: Health Education and Program Planning
PHTH 4540.rationale: The course develops practical health-education interventions through needs assessment, program design, evaluation and budgets; writing and communication support that domain practice.

PHYS 1145.guard: problems in the life and health sciences
PHYS 1145.name: Physics for Life Sciences 1
PHYS 1145.rationale: Mechanics, fluids, temperature and kinetic theory are studied through life- and health-science physical problems; the substantive subject is physical science, not mathematical theory alone.

PHYS 1146.name: Lab for PHYS 1145
PHYS 1146.rationale: The laboratory experiments accompany the explicitly reviewed mechanics, fluids and thermal-physics content of PHYS 1145.

PHYS 1151.name: Physics for Engineering 1
PHYS 1151.rationale: The course studies Newtonian mechanics, motion, forces, energy and fluids in engineering physics; calculus is a tool for physical problems, not the principal subject.

PHYS 1152.name: Lab for PHYS 1151
PHYS 1152.rationale: Experiments accompany PHYS 1151 engineering mechanics and fluids; the laboratory subject is physical science.

PHYS 1153.guard: organized approaches and use of mathematical techniques
PHYS 1153.name: Interactive Learning Seminar for PHYS 1151
PHYS 1153.rationale: The seminar solves physical mechanics, equilibrium, dynamics and fluids problems accompanying PHYS 1151; mathematical techniques support those physical models.

PHYS 1161.name: Physics 1
PHYS 1161.rationale: The lecture studies mechanics, fluids and physical principles through science and medicine examples; it is substantive physics despite calculus prerequisites.

PHYS 1162.name: Lab for PHYS 1161
