PHYS 1162.rationale: Experiments accompany the PHYS 1161 mechanics-and-fluids lecture and remain physical-science laboratory practice.

PHYS 1163.name: Recitation for PHYS 1161
PHYS 1163.rationale: The recitation supports interactive problem solving for the reviewed mechanics and fluids of PHYS 1161; zero credit hours do not erase its distinct course identity.

PHYS 1165.name: Physics 2
PHYS 1165.rationale: Electrostatics, circuits, magnetism and electromagnetic waves are physical-science topics; the course is not computing systems or AI.

PHYS 1166.name: Lab for PHYS 1165
PHYS 1166.rationale: The laboratory experiments accompany PHYS 1165 electricity, magnetism and waves.

PHYS 1167.name: Recitation for PHYS 1165
PHYS 1167.rationale: Interactive problem solving accompanies PHYS 1165 electricity, magnetism and waves; this zero-hour recitation is a distinct physical-science record.

PHYS 1191.guard: conceptual and mathematical foundations of theoretical physics
PHYS 1191.name: Foundations of Theoretical Physics
PHYS 1191.rationale: The course develops theoretical physics through dynamics, fields, statistical physics, relativity and quantum theory, focusing on classical mechanics; mathematical foundations serve those physical phenomena.

PHYS 1192.name: Lab for PHYS 1191
PHYS 1192.rationale: Experiments accompany the reviewed theoretical/classical-physics content of PHYS 1191.

PHYS 1193.name: Recitation for PHYS 1191
PHYS 1193.rationale: Interactive problem solving accompanies PHYS 1191 physics; its zero-hour credit value is preserved independently of its subject category.

PHYS 2303.name: Modern Physics
PHYS 2303.rationale: Atomic and nuclear structure, wave-particle duality, spin, solid-state phenomena and relativity are physical-science content.

PHYS 3600.guard: Data are taken to higher precision
PHYS 3600.name: Advanced Physics Laboratory
PHYS 3600.rationale: Advanced experiments in optics, spectroscopy, semiconductors and related physical phenomena are the primary practice; lab-report writing supports that experimental work.

PHYS 3601.name: Classical Dynamics
PHYS 3601.rationale: The course models classical mechanics through kinematics, oscillators, central forces and rigid bodies; mathematical methods support physical dynamics.

PHYS 3602.name: Electricity and Magnetism 1
PHYS 3602.rationale: Electrostatics, materials, induction and Maxwell equations establish electromagnetic physics as the subject, including computational solutions as tools.

PHYS 3603.name: Electricity and Magnetism 2
PHYS 3603.rationale: Electromagnetic waves, radiation, field visualization and relativity continue the physical-science sequence.

PHYS 4115.name: Quantum Mechanics
PHYS 4115.rationale: The subject is quantum physical behavior, wave-particle duality and the hydrogen atom; probability amplitudes and differential equations are methods used to describe that domain.

PHYS 4305.name: Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics
PHYS 4305.rationale: Thermodynamics, entropy, kinetic theory and quantum gases are the physical systems studied through statistical mechanics.

PHYS 5116.guard: complex networks emerging in nature and technology
PHYS 5116.name: Network Science 1
PHYS 5116.rationale: The description centers on analytical, numerical and modeling tools for complex networks, including graph theory and statistical models across biology, computing and social examples; this is network mathematics, not computing infrastructure.

PHYS 5318.name: Principles of Experimental Physics
PHYS 5318.rationale: Detector techniques, signal/noise measurement, microscopy, lasers and quantum optics are modern experimental physics practices; computing-related examples do not make the course computing infrastructure.

POLS 2325.name: Ancient Philosophy and Political Thought
POLS 2325.rationale: The reciprocal cross-listed course examines classical Greek moral, political and metaphysical writings through written textual analysis.

PSYC 1101.guard: psychology as a method of inquiry
PSYC 1101.name: Foundations of Psychology
PSYC 1101.rationale: The course surveys psychological science including behavior, cognition, development, emotion and disorders; biological learning and cognition do not establish artificial intelligence.

PSYC 2320.name: Statistics in Psychological Research
PSYC 2320.rationale: The description explicitly teaches descriptive/inferential statistics, distributions, regression, probability, hypothesis tests and confidence intervals; psychology is the application context.

PSYC 3200.guard: structure and function of the central nervous system
PSYC 3200.name: Clinical Neuroanatomy
PSYC 3200.rationale: Human central-nervous-system structure/function and clinical lesions establish anatomical/neuroscience domain study.

PSYC 3400.name: Personality
PSYC 3400.rationale: Personality development, assessment and psychological theories are the substantive domain; social determinants are one component rather than the sole subject.

PSYC 3402.name: Social Psychology
PSYC 3402.rationale: The source centers social attitudes, attribution, conformity, gender/culture and group processes; these are social analysis within psychology.

PSYC 3404.name: Developmental Psychology
PSYC 3404.rationale: Psychological development across the lifespan integrates cognition, language, emotion and social functioning as domain science.

PSYC 3406.name: Clinical Psychology and Mental Health
PSYC 3406.rationale: Diagnosis, symptom patterns, etiology and treatment of mental disorders establish clinical psychological domain knowledge.

PSYC 3450.name: Learning and Motivation
PSYC 3450.rationale: Operant/Pavlovian conditioning, biological constraints and animal/human motivation are behavioral science, not machine learning despite overlapping terminology.

PSYC 3451.name: Learning Principles and Behavior Analysis
PSYC 3451.rationale: Applied behavior analysis uses conditioning and reinforcement to understand human learning and developmental disorders; reinforcement here is not an AI algorithm.

PSYC 3452.guard: neural and anatomical bases of sensation and perception
PSYC 3452.name: Sensation and Perception
PSYC 3452.rationale: Sensory perception, anatomy, neural bases and development are biological/psychological domain content.

PSYC 3458.guard: relation between brain function and human behavior
PSYC 3458.name: Biological Psychology
PSYC 3458.rationale: The description concerns biological nerve cells, nervous-system structure, movement and human cognition; its small neural networks are not artificial neural networks.

PSYC 3464.name: Psychology of Language
PSYC 3464.rationale: Human language production, comprehension, acquisition and biological bases are psycholinguistic domain science; no computational NLP methods are stated.

PSYC 3466.name: Cognition
PSYC 3466.rationale: Human attention, memory, categorization and problem solving are studied through cognitive theories and experiments; pattern recognition refers to human cognition, not an AI method.

PSYC 3506.guard: physiological and cognitive aspects of fear
PSYC 3506.name: Neuropsychology of Fear
PSYC 3506.rationale: Physiological and cognitive fear mechanisms, brain function and psychiatric disorders define biological/clinical psychological content.

PSYC 3508.guard: how hormones affect behavior and vice versa
PSYC 3508.name: Behavioral Endocrinology
PSYC 3508.rationale: Hormones, brain structure, behavior and mood/cognition/stress are endocrine and psychological domain knowledge.

PSYC 3510.guard: how it affects) our immune system
PSYC 3510.name: Brain, Behavior, and Immunity
PSYC 3510.rationale: Interactions among immune function, brain, behavior and mental illness are biological/clinical domain mechanisms.

PSYC 4510.guard: interactions between drugs, brain, and behavior
PSYC 4510.name: Psychopharmacology
PSYC 4510.rationale: Drug effects, neurotransmission and treatment of neurological/mental disorders are psychopharmacological domain study.

PSYC 4512.guard: how the human brain works to produce higher mental functions
PSYC 4512.name: Neuropsychology
PSYC 4512.rationale: Neurological patients, brain structure, language, memory and plasticity are used to understand human brain functions, not to teach AI models.

PSYC 4514.name: Clinical Neuroscience
PSYC 4514.rationale: Neurobiological/genetic causes and pharmacological management of mental illness form clinical neuroscience content.

PSYC 4540.guard: Emphasizes theory and modeling, not statistics
PSYC 4540.name: Quantitative Topics in Psychology and Behavioral Neuroscience
PSYC 4540.rationale: The source explicitly emphasizes quantitative theory and modeling, including Fourier analysis, signal detection and linear-algebraic models. Neural/cognitive applications do not erase this primary mathematical-methods focus or establish AI.

PSYC 4570.name: Behavioral Genetics
PSYC 4570.rationale: Genetics is used to study biological behavior, sleep, memory and disorders; quantitative genetics remains a domain method rather than evidence of general mathematics or AI.

PSYC 4600.guard: research project of their own creation
PSYC 4600.name: Laboratory in Research Design
PSYC 4600.rationale: The laboratory explicitly teaches design, execution and interpretation of psychological research; the student-selected project applies this stated domain-methods curriculum rather than defining all course content.

PSYC 4604.name: Laboratory in Learning and Motivation
PSYC 4604.rationale: Experiments investigate animal/human learning, memory and decision behavior; data analysis supports behavioral research rather than general computing or AI.

PSYC 4606.name: Laboratory in Biological Psychology
PSYC 4606.rationale: Supervised psychobiological experiments, scientific literature and reports are biological-psychology research methods.

PSYC 4610.guard: research on issues in the psychology of language
PSYC 4610.name: Laboratory in Psycholinguistics
PSYC 4610.rationale: The laboratory studies psychological language processing through experiments, data collection and reports; statistics are tools for this psychological-domain investigation.

PSYC 4612.guard: conducting research on issues in human cognition
PSYC 4612.name: Laboratory in Cognition
PSYC 4612.rationale: Experiments investigate human cognitive functioning; collection and analysis support domain research rather than an AI training task.

PSYC 4614.name: Laboratory in Social Psychology
PSYC 4614.rationale: The laboratory teaches critical reading, experimental testing and communication of social-psychological research; the subject is explicitly social research.

PSYC 4616.guard: methods and areas of personality research
PSYC 4616.name: Laboratory in Personality
PSYC 4616.rationale: Measurement and experimental research on personality establish a specific psychological domain-methods focus.

PSYC 4622.name: Laboratory in Sensation and Perception
PSYC 4622.rationale: Psychophysical experiments study sensory perception with statistical analysis as a tool; this is perception-domain research rather than general statistics instruction.

PSYC 4624.name: Laboratory in Affective Science
PSYC 4624.rationale: The laboratory studies emotions through affective-science theories and experimental methods; writing and team skills support this psychological domain.

PSYC 4628.guard: experimental and observational research across the life span
PSYC 4628.name: Laboratory in Developmental Psychology
PSYC 4628.rationale: Experimental and observational research addresses human development across the lifespan; statistics and presentation support the domain investigation.

PSYC 4656.guard: practice in lab studies of physiological variables
PSYC 4656.name: Seminar in Biological Psychology
PSYC 4656.rationale: Physiological experiments and nervous-system evolution, disorders, attention and memory are biological psychological content.

PSYC 4658.name: Seminar in Psycholinguistics
PSYC 4658.rationale: Although specific semester topics vary, the description expressly restricts the subject to psychology of language, supporting a limited psychological-domain classification rather than AI or a precise topic claim.

PSYC 4660.name: Seminar in Cognition
PSYC 4660.rationale: Topics vary but are explicitly restricted to cognitive psychology; this supports only broad psychological-domain classification, not a precise semester topic or AI methods.

PSYC 4662.name: Seminar in Personality
PSYC 4662.rationale: Selected topics are explicitly in personality psychology, supporting the broad psychological domain without inventing the chosen topic.

PSYC 4664.guard: read original research and theory papers
PSYC 4664.name: Seminar in Social Psychology
PSYC 4664.rationale: Original theory and research papers address social psychology, supporting social-analysis classification while leaving the particular seminar topic unknown.

PSYC 4666.guard: psychotherapy: theory, methods, and outcome research
PSYC 4666.name: Seminar in Clinical Psychology
PSYC 4666.rationale: Psychotherapy theory, methods and outcome research dominate the seminar; ethics and cross-cultural counseling contextualize the clinical practice.

PSYC 4668.guard: sensory, attentional, motivational, and cognitive factors
PSYC 4668.name: Seminar in Sensation and Perception
PSYC 4668.rationale: The seminar explains human sensory perception through physiological and cognitive factors; environmental information extraction does not establish machine perception.

PSYC 4674.name: Seminar in Cognitive Neuroscience
PSYC 4674.rationale: Human cognitive processes and their biological neural substrates define this neuroscience domain; variable topics do not imply AI content.

PSYC 4676.guard: Specific topics may vary by semester
PSYC 4676.name: Seminar in Developmental Psychology
PSYC 4676.rationale: Psychological processes emerging and changing through the lifespan establish developmental-domain theory and methods despite variable offerings.

PSYC 4682.guard: Specific topics may vary by semester
PSYC 4682.name: Seminar in Learning and Motivation
PSYC 4682.rationale: Human/animal behavioral adaptation, cognitive learning processes and motivation are the explicit content; learning terminology does not imply artificial intelligence.

PT 5410.name: Functional Human Neuroanatomy
PT 5410.rationale: Detailed human nervous-system structures and clinical/neurobiological functions are neuroanatomical domain knowledge; biological connectivity is not computing networks.

PT 5411.name: Lab for PT 5410
PT 5411.rationale: Human brain/spinal-cord specimens, stained tissue and MRI support anatomical study and neurological diagnosis; this is not machine image analysis.

SLPA 1101.name: Bridging Minds: Introduction to Speech, Language, and Hearing Sciences
SLPA 1101.rationale: Speech, language and hearing disorders, assessment, treatment and clinical observation are substantive clinical communication-science practice.

SLPA 1102.guard: development of the language system from birth to adolescence
SLPA 1102.name: Language Development
SLPA 1102.rationale: The course studies child language-development mechanisms, developmental assessment and intervention implications across cognitive, motor and social development; the primary subject is developmental speech/language science.

SLPA 1103.guard: physiology of the speech and hearing mechanism
SLPA 1103.name: Anatomy and Physiology of Speech and Hearing Mechanism
SLPA 1103.rationale: The static structure, musculature and physiology of speech/hearing mechanisms are anatomical and physiological domain content.

SLPA 1200.name: Phonetics
SLPA 1200.rationale: Articulatory and perceptual speech-sound properties and transcription of normal/disordered speech are specific phonetic/clinical speech-science practice, not general rhetorical writing.

SLPA 1203.guard: diagnostic tests performed by the audiologist
SLPA 1203.name: Introduction to Audiology
SLPA 1203.rationale: Sound physics, hearing anatomy/physiology, diagnostic tests and rehabilitation establish audiology as the domain.

SLPA 1205.name: Speech and Hearing Science
SLPA 1205.rationale: Speech acoustics, hearing anatomy, psychoacoustics and perception concern the physical/scientific basis of communication.

SLPA 2000.guard: job search strategies through developing resumés
SLPA 2000.name: Introduction to Co-op
SLPA 2000.rationale: The course prepares students for co-op policies, employment searches and workplace situations; clinical-setting examples do not establish a fixed substantive clinical-method curriculum.

SLPA 4219.name: Introduction to Aural Rehabilitation
SLPA 4219.rationale: The course teaches assessment, diagnosis and management of hearing loss through amplification, rehabilitation and accommodations.

SLPA 4500.guard: children and adults with frequently referred language disorders
SLPA 4500.name: Language Disorders across the Life Span
SLPA 4500.rationale: Language-disorder mechanisms, diagnostic/therapeutic interventions and clinical service delivery are the stated domain content.

SLPA 4651.guard: delays and disorders of speech production
SLPA 4651.name: Speech Disorders across the Life Span
SLPA 4651.rationale: Speech production disorders, clinical diagnosis and therapeutic intervention are the primary subject, including developmental and individual/family effects.

SLPA 5107.name: Clinical Procedures
SLPA 5107.rationale: Functional behavioral analysis and experimental clinical assessment/treatment are applied to speech, language and hearing training; the description establishes clinical practice despite variable three-to-four-hour offerings.

SOCL 1000.name: Sociology at Northeastern
SOCL 1000.rationale: The description centers on first-year orientation, university community and academic/interpersonal success skills, rather than a specified sociology-content curriculum.

SOCL 1101.guard: key sociological theories and empirical research
SOCL 1101.name: Introduction to Sociology
SOCL 1101.rationale: Social identities, race/class/gender, industrial capitalism and sociological theories of order, conflict and change are substantive social analysis.

SOCL 1280.name: The Twenty-First-Century Workplace
SOCL 1280.rationale: The course examines organization, labor control, workplace culture, inequalities and technological change through historical and social analysis.

SOCL 2320.name: Statistical Analysis in Sociology
SOCL 2320.rationale: The specified content is statistical theory and practice: descriptive statistics, regression, the central limit theorem, confidence intervals and hypothesis testing.

SOCL 2321.guard: experimental research, field research, survey research
SOCL 2321.name: Research Methods in Sociology
SOCL 2321.rationale: Experimental, field, survey and historical-comparative research are studied as sociological ways of producing evidence, with ethics and values; the description does not establish primarily mathematical theory.

SOCL 2485.name: Environment, Technology, and Society
SOCL 2485.rationale: The course analyzes relationships among states, societies, science/technology development and environmental conditions through social theory and history.

SOCL 3300.name: Social Theory
SOCL 3300.rationale: Classical and contemporary sociological theoretical traditions and their historical connections are the explicit subject.

SOCL 4528.guard: social and political context of technological change
SOCL 4528.name: Technology and Society
SOCL 4528.rationale: The course analyzes social/political contexts of technological change and institutional responses to the internet and AI; technologies are objects of social analysis, not AI implementation methods.

SOCL 4600.name: Senior Seminar
SOCL 4600.rationale: Students conduct original research on a topic of their choice; collaborative research and writing practices are stated but the selected substantive subject is not fixed.
